equations.name: Coefficient of Determination (R²)
equations.html: R² = 1 − Σ(yᵢ − ŷᵢ)²Σ(yᵢ − ȳ)² = 1 − SSresSStot
where: yᵢ = true output for point i
ŷᵢ = predicted output for point i
ȳ = mean of all true outputs
equations.note: R² = 1 is perfect. R² = 0 means the model performs no better than predicting the mean. R² < 0 means the model is actively worse than predicting the mean.

equations.name: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
equations.html: RMSE = √1n Σ(yᵢ − ŷᵢ)²
equations.note: RMSE is in the same units as the output. It penalises large individual errors more than MAE.

equations.name: Mean Absolute Error (MAE)
equations.html: MAE = 1n Σ |yᵢ − ŷᵢ|
equations.note: MAE is the average absolute error in output units. More robust to outliers than RMSE.

equations.name: Min-Max Normalisation
equations.html: x′ = x − xminxmax − xmin
where: x<sub>min</sub>, x<sub>max</sub> = column minimum and maximum (from training data)
equations.note: Scales every input column to [0, 1]. Sensitive to outliers that extend the range.

equations.name: Z-Score Normalisation
where: σ = column standard deviation (from training data)
x′ = standardised value with mean 0 and std 1
equations.note: More robust to outliers than min-max when the column has extreme values that would compress the rest of the range. Both methods work well with GPR; the toolkit exercises use min-max for bounded engineering parameters.

equations.name: IQR Outlier Bounds
equations.html: Flag if x < Q1 − k·IQR   or   x > Q3 + k·IQR
equations.note: Resistant to extreme values because Q1 and Q3 are not affected by the outliers being detected.

equations.name: GPR Posterior Mean
equations.html: μ*(x*) = K(x*, X) · [K(X, X) + αI]<sup>−1</sup> · y
where: K(x*, X) = covariance vector between x* and all training points
equations.note: This is the prediction. The model weights each training point's contribution by how similar it is to x* (via the kernel K).

equations.name: GPR Posterior Variance
equations.html: σ²*(x*) = k(x*, x*) − K(x*, X) · [K(X, X) + αI]<sup>−1</sup> · K(X, x*)
where: k(x*, x*) = prior variance at x* (from the kernel)
Second term = variance reduction from observing training data
equations.note: This is the uncertainty estimate. Large σ²* means the prediction is less reliable — the point is far from training data.

equations.name: Sobol First-Order Index (S₁)
where: E[Y | X<sub>i</sub>] = expected output when X<sub>i</sub> is fixed
equations.note: Fraction of output variance explained by X<sub>i</sub> acting alone. S₁ ≤ Sₜ always. Large gap (Sₜ − S₁) indicates strong interactions.

equations.name: Kennedy–O'Hagan Multi-Fidelity
where: ρ = scaling factor (fitted by OLS on HF data)
δ(x) = GP correction term trained on residuals HF − ρ·LF
equations.note: Combines many cheap low-fidelity runs with few expensive high-fidelity runs. Uncertainty estimate propagates through both the LF surrogate and the correction GP.
